newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN INTERNET PROVIDER DENIES SECURITY BREACHED.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN INTERNET PROVIDER DENIES SECURITY BREACHED.

text.p: Belgian Internet service provider Belgium Online admitted on Tuesday that reporters had managed to obtain confidential information but denied that its security system had been breached.
It said in a statement that CM Corporate magazine had managed to go up to a "certain level of information" but noted the consulted files could not be manipulated.
"Belgium Online regrets this incident, due to a human error, but confirms that it has no impact on the security of transactions and authentication system of the network," it said in a statement.

CM Corporate said in its latest edition it gained access to confidential records in the website of Beroepskrediet, which wants to offer Belgium Online the possibility of banking via the Internet, the Financeel Economsche Tijd newspaper said.
CM Corporate said its reporters found records with account numbers of Beroepskrediet, lists of transactions and confidential facts of a number of Belgium Online subscribers.
Belgium Online, which was launched last year as a secure platform for transactions over the Internet, said it had taken steps to prevent similar human errors in the future.
